festivals.name: Pausha Putrada Ekadashi
festivals.about: Kept by couples hoping for a child.

festivals.name: Vaikunta (Mukkoti) Ekadashi
festivals.about: The northern gate of Vishnu's temples opens — Srirangam, Tirupati and Udupi. Falls once or twice a year, and some years not at all.

festivals.name: Arudra Darisanam · Thiruvathira
festivals.about: Shiva's cosmic dance, seen at Chidambaram on Ardra in Margazhi; Kerala keeps it as Thiruvathira.

festivals.name: Pausha Purnima
festivals.about: Magh snan begins; the Kumbh's first bathing day.

festivals.name: Lohri
festivals.about: Bonfires, sesame and harvest songs on the night before Makar Sankranti (Punjab).

festivals.name: Bhogi
festivals.about: Old things burn in a dawn bonfire and the Pongal festival begins.

festivals.name: Magh Bihu · Bhogali Bihu
festivals.about: Assam's harvest feast, with the Meji bonfire.

festivals.name: Makar Sankranti · Pongal
festivals.about: The Sun enters Capricorn — kites, til, harvest.

festivals.name: Mattu Pongal · Kanuma
festivals.about: The day for cattle — bathed, decorated and thanked for the harvest.

festivals.name: Kaanum Pongal · Kanu Pidi
festivals.about: Families picnic by the river; sisters pray for their brothers' well-being.

festivals.name: Vasant Panchami
festivals.about: Saraswati, spring, and yellow.

festivals.name: Advaita Acharya Appearance
festivals.about: The appearance of Shri Advaita Acharya.

festivals.name: Ratha Saptami
festivals.about: The Sun turns his chariot north.

festivals.name: Bhishma Ashtami
festivals.about: The day Bhishma chose to leave his body.

festivals.name: Jaya Ekadashi
festivals.about: Freedom from the curse of a wandering spirit.

festivals.name: Varaha Dwadashi
festivals.about: The appearance of Lord Varahadeva.

festivals.name: Nityananda Trayodashi
festivals.about: The appearance of Shri Nityananda Prabhu.

festivals.name: Thaipusam
festivals.about: Murugan receives the vel; kavadi carried in Tamil Nadu and Malaysia.

festivals.name: Guru Ravidas Jayanti
festivals.about: The birthday of the Bhakti saint Ravidas, on the Magha full moon.

festivals.name: Magha Purnima
festivals.about: Holy dips; the Kumbh's big bathing day.

festivals.name: Keddasa
festivals.about: Three days when the earth is said to menstruate; no digging or ploughing.

festivals.name: Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Appearance
festivals.about: The appearance of Shrila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura.

festivals.name: Kumbha Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Aquarius

festivals.name: Maha Shivaratri
festivals.about: The great night of Shiva.

festivals.name: Phulera Dooj
festivals.about: Braj begins its Holi season with flowers.

festivals.name: Amalaki Ekadashi
festivals.about: The amla tree worshipped as Vishnu's dwelling.

festivals.name: Attukal Pongala
festivals.about: Lakhs of women cook sweet pongala for Bhadrakali in Thiruvananthapuram, on Pooram.

festivals.name: Holika Dahan
festivals.about: The bonfire the night before Holi.

festivals.name: Gaura Purnima
festivals.about: The appearance of Shri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

festivals.name: Holi
festivals.about: Colours, water, and no rules.

festivals.name: Sant Tukaram Beej
festivals.about: The day Sant Tukaram is remembered as going to Vaikuntha, observed at Dehu.

festivals.name: Rangpanchami
festivals.about: Holi's last day of colour, five days on (Maharashtra, MP).

festivals.name: Meena Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Pisces

festivals.name: Sheetala Saptami
festivals.about: Cold food for the goddess of healing (Gujarat, Rajasthan).

festivals.name: Shitala Ashtami
festivals.about: Basoda — cold food offered to the goddess Shitala.

festivals.name: Papmochani Ekadashi
festivals.about: The last Ekadashi of the lunar year.

festivals.name: Chaitra Navratri begins
festivals.about: Spring Navratri; nine nights of the Goddess before Ram Navami.

festivals.name: Ugadi · Gudi Padwa
festivals.about: Lunar new year in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana; Chaitra Navratri begins.

festivals.name: Cheti Chand
festivals.about: Sindhi new year and the birth of Jhulelal.

festivals.name: Chaitra Gauri · Haldi Kunku begins
festivals.about: A month of Gauri worship with haldi-kunku gatherings for married women, ending on Akshaya Tritiya.

festivals.name: Gangaur
festivals.about: Rajasthan's festival of Gauri, marital happiness and spring.

festivals.name: Matsya Jayanti
festivals.about: Vishnu's first avatar, the fish who saved the Vedas.

festivals.name: Ramanujacharya Jayanti
festivals.about: The appearance of Shri Ramanujacharya.

festivals.name: Yamuna Jayanti
festivals.about: The river Yamuna's descent to earth.

festivals.name: Navapada Oli begins
festivals.about: Nine days of simple ayambil meals and prayer to the nine padas (Jain).

festivals.name: Ashoka Ashtami
festivals.about: Durga Ashtami of the spring Navratri.

festivals.name: Ram Navami
festivals.about: Rama's birthday, celebrated at midday.

festivals.name: Anang Trayodashi
festivals.about: A spring day for Kamadeva and Rati, kept for love and a happy marriage.

festivals.name: Mahavir Jayanti
festivals.about: The birth of Mahavira, the 24th Jain Tirthankara.

festivals.name: Panguni Uthiram
festivals.about: Divine weddings — Murugan and Deivanai, Shiva and Parvati — celebrated at Tamil temples.

festivals.name: Hanuman Jayanti
festivals.about: Hanuman's birthday on the Chaitra full moon.

festivals.name: Bisu Parba
festivals.about: Tulu new year — the Bisu kani is arranged the night before and seen first thing.

festivals.name: Vishu · Baisakhi · Puthandu · Pohela Boishakh
festivals.about: Solar new year across Kerala, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Bengal, Assam, Odisha.

festivals.name: Varuthini Ekadashi
festivals.about: Protection and prosperity; charity of gold or land.

festivals.name: Somvati Amavasya
festivals.about: A new moon on a Monday — a river dip, and circling the peepal tree 108 times.

festivals.name: Akshaya Tritiya
festivals.about: The never-diminishing day — gold, ventures, weddings.

festivals.name: Parashurama Jayanti
festivals.about: The axe-wielding sixth avatar of Vishnu.

festivals.name: Adi Shankara Jayanti
festivals.about: The philosopher who unified Advaita Vedanta.

festivals.name: Sita Navami
festivals.about: Sita's appearance from the earth, kept at midday.

festivals.name: Narasimha Jayanti
festivals.about: Vishnu's man-lion form, worshipped at twilight.

festivals.name: Buddha Purnima
festivals.about: Birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha.

festivals.name: Kurma Jayanti
festivals.about: Vishnu as the tortoise who bore the churning mountain.

festivals.name: Vrishabha Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Taurus

festivals.name: Apara Ekadashi
festivals.about: Boundless merit; kept before the summer solstice.

festivals.name: Bhaumvati Amavasya
festivals.about: A new moon on a Tuesday — ancestors remembered, Hanuman and Mangal worshipped.

festivals.name: Shani Jayanti
festivals.about: Saturn's birthday; oil offered at Shani temples.

festivals.name: Vat Savitri Amavasya
festivals.about: Savitri's vow, kept on the new moon in North India.

festivals.name: Ganga Dussehra
festivals.about: The Ganga's descent to earth; a dip in the river.

festivals.name: Gayatri Jayanti
festivals.about: The day the Gayatri mantra was revealed.

festivals.name: Nirjala Ekadashi
festivals.about: The strictest Ekadashi — kept without even water; Bhima's Ekadashi.

festivals.name: Pattanaje
festivals.about: Closes the Yakshagana and Bhuta Kola season until the rains pass.

festivals.name: Snana Yatra
festivals.about: The bathing festival of Lord Jagannatha.

festivals.name: Vat Purnima
festivals.about: Savitri's vow — married women circle the banyan tree (Maharashtra, Gujarat).

festivals.name: Mithuna Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Gemini

festivals.name: Jagannath Rath Yatra
festivals.about: Puri's chariot festival.

festivals.name: Devshayani (Ashadhi) Ekadashi
festivals.about: Vishnu begins his four-month sleep and Chaturmas starts; the Pandharpur Wari reaches Vitthal.

festivals.name: Gauri Vrat begins
festivals.about: Five days of fasting by unmarried girls in Gujarat.

festivals.name: Guru Purnima
festivals.about: Honouring teachers; Vyasa's birthday.

festivals.name: Kokila Vrat
festivals.about: Parvati as the cuckoo; a month-long vow that begins on Ashadha Purnima.

festivals.name: Karka Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Cancer

festivals.name: Aati Amavasya
festivals.about: The monsoon new moon — paleda kashaya, a bitter bark drink, is taken at dawn.

festivals.name: Gatari Amavasya
festivals.about: Maharashtra's feast day and Dipa Pooja on Ashadha Amavasya, before vegetarian Shravan begins.

festivals.name: Shravan Somvar begins
festivals.about: The Mondays of Shravan, the most auspicious for Shiva.

festivals.name: Hariyali Teej
festivals.about: Monsoon swings and green saris for Parvati (North India).

festivals.name: Nag Panchami
festivals.about: Serpent worship at the height of the monsoon.

festivals.name: Varalakshmi Vratam
festivals.about: Married women worship Lakshmi on the Friday before Shravana Purnima.

festivals.name: Narali Purnima
festivals.about: Fishing communities offer a coconut to the sea and reopen the waters after the monsoon, on the day Raksha Bandhan falls.

festivals.name: Raksha Bandhan
festivals.about: Siblings' day — the rakhi thread.

festivals.name: Kajari Teej
festivals.about: Monsoon songs and a fast for married women (UP, Bihar, MP).

festivals.name: Krishna Janmashtami
festivals.about: Krishna's birth at midnight.

festivals.name: Dahi Handi
festivals.about: Human pyramids break the pot of curd, as the young Krishna did.

festivals.name: Mosaru Kudike · Vittal Pindi
festivals.about: The day after Janmashtami, Udupi's Krishna Matha breaks the curd pots in its Leelotsava.

festivals.name: Prabhupada Appearance Day
festivals.about: The appearance of Shrila A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada.

festivals.name: Simha Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Leo

festivals.name: Bail Pola · Pithori Amavasya
festivals.about: Farmers honour their oxen; mothers keep Pithori Vrat for their children.

festivals.name: Somvati Amavasya
festivals.about: A new moon on a Monday — a river dip, and circling the peepal tree 108 times.

festivals.name: Onam · Thiruvonam
festivals.about: Kerala's harvest festival — King Mahabali comes home.

festivals.name: Bhaumvati Amavasya
festivals.about: A new moon on a Tuesday — ancestors remembered, Hanuman and Mangal worshipped.

festivals.name: Kanya Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Virgo

festivals.name: Koral Parba · Kadiru Habba
festivals.about: The first sheaves of the new rice are cut, offered and eaten. The day varies by family, and Tulu panchangas differ on it.

festivals.name: Hartalika Teej
festivals.about: Parvati's fast to win Shiva.

festivals.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
festivals.about: Ganesha comes home for ten days.

festivals.name: Rishi Panchami
festivals.about: Honouring the seven sages; kept after Hartalika Teej.

festivals.name: Gauri Avahana
festivals.about: Jyeshtha Gauri is welcomed home during Ganeshotsav, on Anuradha nakshatra.

festivals.name: Gauri Pujan
festivals.about: The main worship of Gauri, with a feast, on Jyeshtha nakshatra.

festivals.name: Gauri Visarjan
festivals.about: Gauri is sent off, on Mula nakshatra.

festivals.name: Mahalakshmi Vrat begins
festivals.about: Sixteen days of fasting for Lakshmi.

festivals.name: Radha Ashtami
festivals.about: Radha's birthday, fifteen days after Krishna's.

festivals.name: Vamana Jayanti
festivals.about: Vishnu as the dwarf who measured the worlds in three steps.

festivals.name: Bhaktivinoda Thakura Appearance
festivals.about: The appearance of Shrila Bhaktivinoda Thakura.

festivals.name: Anant Chaturdashi
festivals.about: Ganesh visarjan; Vishnu as Anant.

festivals.name: Pitru Paksha begins
festivals.about: A fortnight for ancestors.

festivals.name: Jivitputrika (Jitiya)
festivals.about: Mothers fast without water for their children (Bihar, UP, Jharkhand).

festivals.name: Bathukamma begins
festivals.about: Telangana's nine days of flower stacks for the goddess begin on Mahalaya Amavasya and end at Saddula Bathukamma.

festivals.name: Mahalaya Amavasya
festivals.about: Pitru Paksha ends; Durga is invited (Bengal).

festivals.name: Sharad Navratri begins
festivals.about: Nine nights of the Goddess; Ghatasthapana.

festivals.name: Tula Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Libra

festivals.name: Maha Shashthi
festivals.about: Durga Puja begins — the goddess is welcomed at Bodhon.

festivals.name: Navratri Saraswati Puja
festivals.about: Books, instruments and tools are worshipped on the Mula nakshatra of Navratri.

festivals.name: Maha Saptami
festivals.about: The goddess is installed with Nabapatrika, the nine-plant bathing.

festivals.name: Navapada Oli begins
festivals.about: Nine days of simple ayambil meals and prayer to the nine padas (Jain).

festivals.name: Durga Ashtami
festivals.about: The eighth night — Maha Ashtami, kanya puja.

festivals.name: Ayudha Puja
festivals.about: Tools, books and vehicles are cleaned and worshipped on Navami, in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Tulu Nadu.

festivals.name: Maha Navami
festivals.about: The ninth night; Ayudha Puja in the South.

festivals.name: Dussehra · Vijayadashami
festivals.about: Good over evil — Ravana burns, Durga returns.

festivals.name: Kojagari Lakshmi Puja
festivals.about: Lakshmi is worshipped at home and the household stays awake under the full moon; in Maharashtra, spiced milk is shared.

festivals.name: Sharad Purnima
festivals.about: Kojagiri — kheer under the brightest moon.

festivals.name: Valmiki Jayanti
festivals.about: The birthday of Maharishi Valmiki, composer of the Ramayana.

festivals.name: Karwa Chauth
festivals.about: A day-long fast broken at moonrise (North India).

festivals.name: Ahoi Ashtami
festivals.about: Mothers fast for their children (North India).

festivals.name: Govatsa Dwadashi
festivals.about: Vasu Baras — cows and calves honoured as Diwali opens.

festivals.name: Dhanteras
festivals.about: Diwali begins — buy something metal.

festivals.name: Narak Chaturdashi · Choti Diwali
festivals.about: Krishna defeats Narakasura; the oil bath before dawn.

festivals.name: Diwali · Lakshmi Puja
festivals.about: The festival of lights, on the darkest night.

festivals.name: Kali Puja
festivals.about: Bengal and Odisha worship Kali at midnight on the new moon, the same night most of India lights Diwali lamps.

festivals.name: Govardhan Puja · Bali Pratipada
festivals.about: Krishna lifts the hill; Gujarati new year.

festivals.name: Bhai Dooj
festivals.about: Sisters host brothers; Diwali's last day.

festivals.name: Vrishchika Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Scorpio

festivals.name: Chhath: Nahay Khay
festivals.about: Chhath begins with a holy bath and a simple meal.

festivals.name: Chhath: Kharna
festivals.about: A day-long fast broken at dusk with kheer, before the 36-hour waterless fast.

festivals.name: Chhath Puja
festivals.about: Sun worship at the river (Bihar, UP, Jharkhand).

festivals.name: Kanda Sashti
festivals.about: Six days for Murugan, ending in the defeat of Surapadman.

festivals.name: Chhath: Usha Arghya
festivals.about: Offerings to the rising Sun end the Chhath fast.

festivals.name: Akshaya Navami
festivals.about: Amla Navami — a meal eaten under the gooseberry tree.

festivals.name: Gopashtami
festivals.about: Krishna became a cowherd; cows are decorated and fed.

festivals.name: Kansa Vadh
festivals.about: Krishna's defeat of his uncle Kansa, marked in Mathura.

festivals.name: Prabodhini (Devutthana) Ekadashi
festivals.about: Vishnu wakes, Chaturmas ends and the season of weddings and Tulsi Vivah begins.

festivals.name: Tulsi Vivah
festivals.about: The tulsi plant is married to Vishnu; wedding season opens.

festivals.name: Vaikuntha Chaturdashi
festivals.about: Shiva and Vishnu worshipped together at midnight.

festivals.name: Guru Nanak Jayanti · Gurpurab
festivals.about: The birthday of Guru Nanak, the first Sikh Guru, on Kartik Purnima.

festivals.name: Karthigai Deepam
festivals.about: Tamil Nadu's festival of lamps; a great fire on Thiruvannamalai.

festivals.name: Kartik Purnima · Dev Deepawali
festivals.about: The gods' Diwali on the ghats; Guru Nanak Jayanti.

festivals.name: Kalabhairav Jayanti
festivals.about: Shiva's fierce form, worshipped at midnight.

festivals.name: Utpanna Ekadashi
festivals.about: The Ekadashi on which Ekadashi herself was born.

festivals.name: Sant Dnyaneshwar Sanjivan Samadhi
festivals.about: Sant Dnyaneshwar's samadhi at Alandi; the end of the Kartiki Wari for the Varkaris.

festivals.name: Dhanu Sankranti
festivals.about: The day the Sun enters Sagittarius

festivals.name: Vivah Panchami
festivals.about: The wedding of Rama and Sita, kept in Janakpur and Ayodhya.

festivals.name: Champa Shashthi (Khandoba)
festivals.about: The last of Khandoba's six-day festival — turmeric, dry coconut and brinjal offered to the family deity.

festivals.name: Subrahmanya Shashthi
festivals.about: Kukke Subrahmanya's car festival and the serpent pilgrimage in coastal Karnataka; the same tithi Maharashtra keeps for Khandoba.

festivals.name: Gita Jayanti
festivals.about: The day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken.

festivals.name: Vaikunta (Mukkoti) Ekadashi
festivals.about: The northern gate of Vishnu's temples opens — Srirangam, Tirupati and Udupi. Falls once or twice a year, and some years not at all.

festivals.name: Annapurna Jayanti
festivals.about: The goddess who feeds everyone; kitchens are honoured.

festivals.name: Dattatreya Jayanti
festivals.about: The three-in-one guru.

festivals.name: Arudra Darisanam · Thiruvathira
festivals.about: Shiva's cosmic dance, seen at Chidambaram on Ardra in Margazhi; Kerala keeps it as Thiruvathira.
